usageNotes: Use this to define a cluster-wide custom CPU model that VMs can reference by name, allowing you to lock in a specific CPU baseline with additional feature flags independent of host CPU changes. Requires the `Mapping.Modify` privilege on `/mapping/cpu`. The `cputype` name is stored without the `custom-` prefix internally, but VMs reference it as `custom-<name>`; omit the prefix when calling this endpoint and Proxmox will normalize it.

examples.summary: Create a hardened Skylake-Server custom CPU model with security mitigations enabled

tips: The `cputype` value must conform to pve-configid format (alphanumeric plus hyphens/underscores, max 40 chars); keep names short since VMs will reference them as `custom-<name>`.
Setting `phys-bits` to `host` improves performance but breaks live migration to hosts with different physical address bit widths — use an explicit numeric value for migrateable VMs.
Setting `level` to 30 is a well-known workaround for Hyper-V boot failures on Windows guests running on recent Intel hosts.
The `hidden` flag suppresses KVM identification and can help with guest software that behaves differently in virtualized environments, but only affects x86-64 vCPUs.
Flags prefixed with `+` enable a feature; `-` disables it. The special alias `nested-virt` maps to `svm` (AMD) or `vmx` (Intel) automatically.
This endpoint returns null on success — validate creation by calling GET /cluster/qemu/custom-cpu-models afterward.
